summary: Latvia is a unitary state in which the Saeima sets every tax and the State Revenue Service collects almost all of them. The two largest flows are VAT and the 34.09% social insurance contributions. The personal income tax is a state tax, but most of its revenue goes to the municipalities of residence; the municipalities’ own tax is the property tax. Company profit is taxed only when it is distributed.
structureNote: The figures are the Commission’s National Tax List for 2024. The personal income tax is drawn twice, as the State’s and the municipalities’ share, using Eurostat’s split of the same year. The sale of emission permits (EUR 90.8 million), the employers’ imputed social contributions (EUR 248.3 million) and the Riga tourist fee (EUR 1.75 million, the only municipal fee the list itemises) are left out. The social contributions are drawn under the State, which collects them for the State Social Insurance Agency.

theme.motifNote: Topographic contour lines over the outline of Latvia (the generic motif; no bespoke art yet).

levels.description: The Saeima legislates all taxes; the State Revenue Service (VID) collects them and the mandatory state social insurance contributions, which fund pensions and other benefits through the State Social Insurance Agency.
levels.fiscalPower: Rates and bases of all taxes are fixed by law in the Saeima; municipalities cannot create taxes.

levels.description: The only tier below the State. They receive most of the personal income tax paid by their residents, levy the immovable property tax within the range set by law, and charge a few local duties.
levels.fiscalPower: Municipalities set the property tax rate within the limits fixed by the national law; the share of the personal income tax is fixed by law.

denominators.label: State taxes (National Tax List), 2024
denominators.definition: The taxes on production and imports, on income and on capital that the National Tax List books to the State and the EU, other than the municipal lines and the sale of emission permits; includes the State’s part of the personal income tax.
denominators.locator: Sheet LV, 2024, the lines listed with each tax
denominators.calculation: Sum of the 16 tax rows below (EUR million)
denominators.caveat: Calendar 2024; the list's cut-off was 30 October 2025. Vintage check against Eurostat's July 2026 accounts: D2: NTL 5,913.03, Eurostat July 2026 5,913; D5: NTL 3,733.2, Eurostat July 2026 3,733.2; D61: NTL 4,668.86, Eurostat July 2026 4,668.9.

denominators.label: Mandatory state social insurance contributions, 2024
denominators.definition: The actual compulsory social contributions of employers, employees and the self-employed, and voluntary contributions; imputed contributions are left out.
denominators.locator: Sheet LV, 2024, lines D611, D613CE, D613CS and D613V
denominators.calculation: Sum of the social contribution rows below (EUR million)
denominators.caveat: Calendar 2024, same list and cut-off as the taxes.

denominators.label: Personal income tax received by the municipalities, 2024
denominators.definition: The part of the personal income tax that Eurostat’s accounts record under local government.
denominators.caveat: Eurostat July 2026 vintage, a different release from the National Tax List.

denominators.label: Own taxes of the municipalities, 2024
denominators.locator: Sheet LV, 2024, lines D29A C01 and C03
denominators.calculation: Sum of the local rows below (EUR million)
denominators.caveat: Eurostat books EUR 257.7 million of taxes on production to local government and the National Tax List itemises EUR 237.34 million; EUR 17 million of the natural resource and permit revenue is attributed to local government by Eurostat but not itemised in the list.

sizing.label: Taxes and compulsory social contributions of all levels of government
sizing.definition: The taxes of the State and the municipalities plus the actual social contributions, calendar 2024, as listed in the National Tax List and split by Eurostat. Excludes the sale of emission permits, imputed social contributions and the Riga tourist fee.
